evaluations.evidence: search and discover music using content identification or fingerprinting
evaluations.rationale: Scope is broad (search + discovery) and the capability implied by “content identification/fingerprinting” could range from simple lookup to full fingerprinting pipeline and matching at scale, making estimation difficult without further boundaries.

evaluations.evidence: search and discover music based on my profile
evaluations.rationale: Underspecified what “based on my profile” entails (which attributes, algorithm, UI/UX, personalization depth), so implementation effort could vary widely.

evaluations.evidence: based on other users similar to myself
evaluations.rationale: Similarity definition, data sources, and recommendation/search behavior are unspecified, leading to a wide range of possible implementations and estimates.

evaluations.evidence: music or ringback tones similar to a given music video based on content similarity
evaluations.rationale: Cross-media similarity (video to music/ringback tones) is complex and underspecified (features, similarity method, outputs), making it hard to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: exploiting enriched metadata and image tags... find related artists, new genre, or other relevant listening path
evaluations.rationale: Very broad discovery/navigation requirement with unclear boundaries (“other relevant listening path”), unclear data enrichment and tagging scope, so estimation is unreliable.

evaluations.evidence: upload tagged videos and have tags available for all further processing steps
evaluations.rationale: “All further processing steps” is open-ended and depends on unspecified downstream pipeline components, making scope too broad to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: view thumbnail sequences of video segments
evaluations.rationale: A reasonably bounded UI capability (display thumbnails for segments) that can be estimated without needing detailed design.

evaluations.evidence: get info about similar video items and segments
evaluations.rationale: “Similar” and “info” are undefined (similarity basis, what information, how presented), so the implementation could vary greatly.

evaluations.evidence: info about perceptually similar video items and segments
evaluations.rationale: Perceptual similarity can imply complex CV/AV algorithms; outputs and constraints are not specified, making estimation difficult.

evaluations.evidence: receive content recommendations from similar profiles
evaluations.rationale: Recommendation logic, definition of “similar profiles,” and delivery mechanism are unspecified, leading to wide estimation variance.

evaluations.evidence: recommendations based on most relevant news events in my area
evaluations.rationale: Requires defining “relevant news events,” sourcing news, geolocation, and recommendation behavior; too underspecified for reliable estimation.

evaluations.evidence: identify persons in videos, and receive related information about them
evaluations.rationale: Person identification in video plus “related information” is a large, complex, and underspecified scope (recognition accuracy, databases, privacy), making estimation hard.

evaluations.evidence: identify products in videos, and receive related information about them
evaluations.rationale: Product recognition in video and the nature/source of “related information” are unspecified and potentially very large in scope.

evaluations.evidence: identify broadcaster logos in videos, and receive related information about them
evaluations.rationale: Logo detection might be estimatable, but “receive related information” is undefined and could expand scope significantly, making estimation unreliable.

evaluations.evidence: identify brands in videos, and receive related information about them
evaluations.rationale: Brand identification is broad (many brands, contexts) and “related information” is unspecified, so scope is too open to estimate well.

evaluations.evidence: take a picture or upload an image... recommended with videos related to that picture or image
evaluations.rationale: Image-to-video recommendation is underspecified (matching method, similarity, catalog size, UX), making effort hard to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: walk around, access content using a geographical map and be informed if there are videos covering the area, monuments or any other relevant point of interest
evaluations.rationale: Combines multiple large capabilities (map UI, geofencing, POI detection, “any other relevant” POIs) with unclear boundaries, making estimation difficult.

evaluations.evidence: search content items using automatic speech recognition
evaluations.rationale: ASR-based search could mean integrating an ASR service, building indexing, handling languages/accuracy; scope and constraints are not specified enough for estimation.

evaluations.evidence: see, validate and edit segmentation of videos
evaluations.rationale: A bounded admin workflow (view/validate/edit segment boundaries) that can be reasonably estimated as a feature set.

evaluations.evidence: annotate news video segments and extract a topic for each segment
evaluations.rationale: Mixes manual annotation with “extract a topic” (could be manual selection or automated NLP/topic modeling); unclear approach and scope affects estimability.

evaluations.evidence: filter and rank videos based on A/V quality aspects
evaluations.rationale: “A/V quality aspects” and ranking criteria are unspecified; could range from simple metadata filters to complex signal analysis, making estimation hard.

evaluations.evidence: quick assessment of whether audio material has been edited before the upload
evaluations.rationale: Audio tamper/edit detection is complex and underspecified (what edits, accuracy, method), so effort is difficult to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: prefilter nudity content
evaluations.rationale: Could imply anything from keyword flags to ML-based image/video nudity detection with thresholds and review workflow; insufficiently bounded for estimation.

evaluations.evidence: prefilter content using search based on low­level asset information
evaluations.rationale: “Low-level asset information” and the search/prefilter behavior are vague, leaving too many implementation possibilities to estimate reliably.

evaluations.evidence: automatically validated the ingested contents for copyright infringement
evaluations.rationale: Automated copyright infringement validation is a large, complex domain with unclear method (fingerprinting, licensing DBs, policy), making estimation difficult.

evaluations.evidence: prefilter the content using search on high­level asset information such as metadata and tags either recognized by the system of provided by the user
evaluations.rationale: High-level info sources and search/prefilter rules are not defined; scope could be small or extensive, so estimation is unreliable.

evaluations.evidence: assess how interesting or appealing or complex a picture is based on automated analysis, citizen annotations, and comments on Talk
evaluations.rationale: Multiple subjective constructs (interesting/appealing/complex) and multiple data sources with unspecified model/metrics make scope too vague to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: detect when a scientist should be prompted to look at a subject, based on annotations and information from Talk comments
evaluations.rationale: Trigger conditions, thresholds, and interpretation of comments are unspecified; could require complex ML/NLP and workflow integration, hard to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: identify volunteer types
evaluations.rationale: “Volunteer types” is undefined (taxonomy, criteria, data used), so the scope ranges from simple segmentation to complex behavioral modeling.

evaluations.evidence: preclassify the Galaxy Zoo images using simple low­level image features
evaluations.rationale: Bounded by “simple low-level image features” and a specific dataset context, making it reasonably estimatable as an ML/classification task.

evaluations.evidence: detect Snapshot Serengeti images with no classifiable animals in them
evaluations.rationale: A specific detection task with clear outcome (empty/no classifiable animals) in a defined domain, enabling reasonable estimation.

evaluations.evidence: automatic image series detection for the case of timestamping malfunction
evaluations.rationale: “Image series detection” and what constitutes/handles “timestamping malfunction” are not defined; could involve multiple heuristics and edge cases, making estimation harder.

evaluations.evidence: automatic animal species preclassification in Snapshot Serengeti
evaluations.rationale: Species preclassification is broad (many species, model scope, accuracy targets, training data) and not bounded, making estimation difficult.

evaluations.evidence: automatic animal attribute preclassification in Snapshot Serengeti
evaluations.rationale: “Animal attribute” is undefined (which attributes, labels, granularity), so scope is too open to estimate reliably.

evaluations.evidence: automatic animal number detection in Snapshot Serengeti
evaluations.rationale: Counting animals can range from simple classification bins to precise detection/counting; approach and accuracy expectations are unspecified, affecting estimability.

evaluations.evidence: automatic segmentation or localization of plankton in Plankton Portal
evaluations.rationale: “Segmentation or localization” leaves alternative scopes (pixel-wise segmentation vs bounding boxes) and no constraints/targets, making estimation difficult.

evaluations.evidence: detect Plankton Portal images with no classifiable plankton in them
evaluations.rationale: A specific detection outcome in a defined domain; can be estimated as a classification/filtering task.

evaluations.evidence: automatic detection of plankton size or orientation
evaluations.rationale: “Size or orientation” is ambiguous (measurement definition, units, precision, method), so scope is insufficiently specified for estimation.

evaluations.evidence: automatic preclassification of plankton species
evaluations.rationale: Species set, label granularity, and performance expectations are not specified; could be small or very large scope, making estimation difficult.

evaluations.evidence: perform automatic worm motion analysis to reduce video duration
evaluations.rationale: “Motion analysis” and how it reduces duration (summarization rules, thresholds, outputs) are underspecified, leading to broad implementation possibilities.

evaluations.evidence: detect the time... where the worm lays an egg
evaluations.rationale: Event detection in video is complex and lacks constraints (accuracy, annotation availability, definition of event time), making estimation difficult.

evaluations.evidence: detect important features such as areas of flooding, damage, temporary shelters, blocked roads etc in the satellite images
evaluations.rationale: Multiple feature types (“etc”) with unclear list, definitions, and detection requirements create a broad, expanding scope that is hard to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: assess the probability/weight of a volunteer’s classification based on their experience
evaluations.rationale: Weighting model, definition of “experience,” and how weights are used are unspecified; could be simple heuristics or complex modeling, affecting estimability.

evaluations.evidence: prefiltering of the images to remove artefacts such as bright stars and camera read errors
evaluations.rationale: “Artefacts such as” implies an open-ended set; methods and thresholds are unspecified, so scope can expand and is hard to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: detect moving and transient objects in the images
evaluations.rationale: “Moving and transient objects” is broad and depends on data type (single images vs time series), definitions, and detection approach; insufficiently bounded for estimation.

evaluations.evidence: remove background noise and distracting sounds from the audio files
evaluations.rationale: Audio cleanup scope is vague (“distracting sounds”), with no constraints on quality, types of noise, or processing method, making estimation difficult.

evaluations.evidence: group whale calls that are similar
evaluations.rationale: Similarity definition, grouping method (clustering, classification), and expected outputs are unspecified, leading to wide estimation variance.

evaluations.evidence: identify the number of whales heard in a single audio file
evaluations.rationale: Counting whales from audio is complex and lacks constraints (species, overlapping calls, accuracy), making estimation difficult.

evaluations.evidence: know when I should interrupt a volunteer
evaluations.rationale: Decision logic for “should interrupt” is undefined (triggers, goals, channels), making scope too vague to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: know whether I should interrupt a volunteer with text, an image, or a video
evaluations.rationale: Requires defining interruption strategy and selection criteria among modalities; without rules/constraints, scope is underspecified and hard to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: know when I should educate a volunteer
evaluations.rationale: “Should educate” lacks defined triggers, objectives, and measurement; could entail complex personalization, making estimation difficult.

evaluations.evidence: know whether I should educate a volunteer with text, an image, or a video
evaluations.rationale: Modality selection criteria and education workflow are unspecified, so implementation scope is unclear and hard to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: know which piece of education I should give to a volunteer
evaluations.rationale: Requires defining the education content set, recommendation/selection logic, and context signals; too underspecified for estimation.

evaluations.evidence: know when a volunteer has made an interesting comment on a subject
evaluations.rationale: “Interesting comment” is subjective and undefined; detection could range from simple keyword rules to advanced NLP, making estimation difficult.

evaluations.evidence: know when Zoonibot should comment on a subject
evaluations.rationale: Bot commenting policy, triggers, and constraints are unspecified; scope could be minimal or extensive, so estimation is hard.

evaluations.evidence: know when Zoonibot should give an explanation
evaluations.rationale: Explanation triggers and content generation approach are unspecified, leading to broad possible implementations and poor estimability.

evaluations.evidence: know what Zoonibot should say to a volunteer
evaluations.rationale: Open-ended natural language generation/content selection requirement without constraints, making scope extremely broad and hard to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: group subjects by similarity
evaluations.rationale: Similarity basis, subject type, and grouping outputs are unspecified; could be simple metadata grouping or complex ML, making estimation difficult.

evaluations.evidence: recommend different projects to volunteers based on their previous experiences
evaluations.rationale: Recommendation inputs (“previous experiences”), algorithm, and delivery are not defined; scope can vary widely, hindering estimation.

evaluations.evidence: see a summary of articles, so that I reuse them
evaluations.rationale: “Summary of articles” is underspecified (which articles, summary type/length, generation method, UI), so effort could range from simple list to NLP summarization.
